strategy.lead: A shared dwelling, made expressive through the response of praise. The containing space and the gesture of opening, gathering, or lifting should belong to the same form.
strategy.principle: The name should be recognized before the explanation is known. The explanation should deepen a strong form, rather than rescue an arbitrary one.

findings.title: Dwelling among a people
findings.text: Exodus 25:8 links sanctuary with dwelling “among them.” Design for a relationship between sacred dwelling and people, rather than real estate alone.

findings.title: Presence is more than an icon
findings.text: Exodus 40 describes the cloud covering the Tent of Meeting and glory filling the tabernacle. Light, an opening, or a held interior would be contemporary artistic interpretations, not a graphic depiction of God.

findings.title: Entering with thanksgiving
findings.text: Psalm 100 connects gladness, singing, entering, thanksgiving, praise, and belonging. A threshold can explore invitation without pretending to reconstruct the wilderness sanctuary.

findings.title: Praise extends beyond music
findings.text: Psalm 150 names several instruments, dancing, and everything that has breath. The parish identity need not be led by any one instrument.

findings.title: Context matters
findings.text: Hebrews 9 describes earthly sanctuary arrangements and restricted priestly access, then develops its Christological argument. It is not a logo blueprint or a mandate for literal furniture.

findings.title: Joined material, one dwelling
findings.text: Exodus 26–27 and Numbers 4 describe joined textiles, covering, frames, screens, court, and transport. Coupling and a shared interior offer a fresh construction language. Historical reconstruction and archaeological claims remain outside the verified evidence.

territories.title: The Dwelling of Praise
territories.intent: Can the covering itself become an act of uplift? Joined textile and an expressive interior form one gesture.
territories.risk: A roof with another worship icon placed underneath.

territories.title: Enter His Courts
territories.intent: Can access and thanksgiving become one generous spatial movement? Investigate threshold and response.
territories.risk: Generic gates, a maze, an exclusive fortress, or a false historical-access claim.

territories.title: The Presence Within
territories.intent: Can the interior matter more than the container? Explore attention, an opening, and meaningful negative space.
territories.risk: Claiming a white void, flame, or ray is a literal depiction of God.

territories.title: One House, Many Voices
territories.intent: Can distinct contributions make one shared dwelling? Make the parts interdependent, with a generous common center.
territories.risk: People around a circle, a flower, stick figures, or a networking icon.

territories.title: A Dwelling that Sings
territories.intent: Can architectural or textile rhythm carry praise without an instrument? The structure supplies the cadence.
territories.risk: Harp strings under a new name, an equalizer, or an arbitrary skyline.

territories.title: The Living Wordmark
territories.intent: Can the complete name carry the identity through letter relationships, shared structure, and readable expression?
territories.risk: Illegible ligatures, decorative bounce, or an oversized initial that overpowers the name.

sketches.name: Responsive Cover
sketches.idea: Joined textile folds make a dwelling whose own lifted edges express response and praise.
sketches.approach: Pictorial material fusion / generous negative interior
construction: Two substantial, asymmetric curved panels, not an arch with a separate figure.
The space held between the panels is part of the construction.
sketches.risk: The organic embrace can suggest a general care charity; the covering is abstract.
sketches.why: Tested as a research-led hypothesis before shortlist selection.
sketches.reason: Advances because the covering and its upward response are the same draped construction. It offers the most direct dwelling association without a separate worship icon.

sketches.name: Coupled Fabric
sketches.idea: Separate textile lengths become one woven dwelling through a visible over-and-under relationship.
construction: Broad orthogonal textile lengths turn around a shared center.
Alternating interruptions suggest coupling rather than extra ornament.
sketches.risk: Its woven logic can look like an industrial or technology monogram.
sketches.why: Tested as a research-led hypothesis before shortlist selection.
sketches.reason: Set aside: the coupled lengths look like an industrial/technology monogram; the meaningful textile premise is better expressed by 01.

sketches.name: Processional Court
sketches.idea: A generous open perimeter brings entering and a common interior into one plan-like sign.
construction: One continuous court perimeter with a broad unclosed threshold.
Two interior panels establish rhythm without drawing worshippers.
sketches.risk: Could read as a maze, venue plan, or a closed institution; literal sanctuary access is not implied.
sketches.why: Tested as a research-led hypothesis before shortlist selection.
sketches.reason: Set aside: its literal plan becomes a rigid venue/maze-like sign and the internal panels can look like a face. It is less welcoming than the brief requires.

sketches.name: Returning Thanks
sketches.idea: A continuous spatial gesture enters, gathers, and turns outward: thanksgiving as a response rather than a gate icon.
construction: A single broad path folds from enclosure into an open outward return.
No discrete doorway, arrow, person, or musical symbol is added.
sketches.risk: A continuous return can read as a letter or a general wayfinding symbol.
sketches.why: Tested as a research-led hypothesis before shortlist selection.
sketches.reason: Set aside: the return reads as a P/e or wayfinding sign before it communicates thanksgiving. The explanation would carry too much of the idea.

sketches.name: Held Light
sketches.idea: A substantial surrounding form gives a white interior room to open upward, exploring presence through attention to space.
construction: Two curved masses hold one continuous white interior, open at top and base.
The opening is material absence; it is not labeled as God.
sketches.risk: A vessel, flame, or seed is an alternative reading. Divine presence cannot be reduced to a white aperture.
sketches.why: Tested as a research-led hypothesis before shortlist selection.
sketches.reason: Set aside: the apparent flame or seed overwhelms the intended held interior. A white aperture must not be labeled as a depiction of God.

sketches.name: Room in the Veil
sketches.idea: The meeting of folded screens makes a luminous room rather than a façade; the unseen interior becomes the focal point.
construction: Offset screen planes hold a larger unfilled chamber and a secondary inner fold.
The geometry is a contemporary spatial abstraction, not a historical reconstruction.
sketches.risk: A portal or architectural app symbol may dominate; extra inner detail may weaken the essential idea.
sketches.why: Tested as a research-led hypothesis before shortlist selection.
sketches.reason: Set aside: the hard portal and inner fragment feel like an architectural software icon. Its internal detail adds complexity without clearer meaning.

sketches.name: Common Ground
sketches.idea: Unequal broad surfaces depend on one another to make a single generous room; gathering creates the dwelling.
construction: Four unequal filled surfaces describe a shared room in an abstract oblique view.
The room and its front opening are actual transparent space; its perimeter belongs to all the parts.
Height and curve vary between contributions without introducing heads, figures, or a central leader.
The number of components is compositional, with no theological claim.
sketches.risk: Can read as a vessel or amphitheater rather than a sacred dwelling; narrow upper seams need proof at 16px.
sketches.why: Strongest of the collective studies: the room exists because the contributions cooperate, and the silhouette avoids a crown or ring of people.
sketches.reason: Advances because interdependent surfaces visibly make one shared room; the generous opening gives belonging a spatial form rather than a ring of people.

sketches.name: A Common Centre
sketches.idea: Unequal organic contributions orient toward one generous shared interior rather than orbiting a leader or figure.
construction: Five broad, unequal curved surfaces gather around an off-center open room.
Separate pieces leave visible joints and a generous lower opening.
The shared interior is transparent space, not a representation of God.
sketches.risk: The lobed perimeter may read as a flower or a generic community organization; the assembly is less immediately memorable than 07.
sketches.why: Provides a soft welcoming counterpoint, but should be set aside unless the parish strongly prefers an organic gathering over architectural clarity.
sketches.reason: Set aside: the organic center reads too much like a generic community flower. Softness alone does not establish a parish identity.

sketches.name: Cadenced Wall
sketches.idea: A folded wall changes height and turns around a shared forecourt; the structure itself carries an expressive cadence.
construction: Five broad faces form a long pleated architectural surface, with different widths and heights.
The top and lower edges change together to describe a turned wall rather than independent equalizer bars.
Transparent triangular seams articulate the folds; the forecourt remains open in front of them.
This is a modern architectural metaphor, not a reconstruction of the biblical tabernacle.
sketches.risk: Can suggest a cultural venue or civic building; its width and creases are less robust as a tiny avatar than a compact silhouette.
sketches.why: A credible non-instrument test of a dwelling that sings: rhythm belongs to the material and scale of the enclosure.
sketches.reason: Advances as a genuinely different, architectural way to test praise through cadence. Broad folded faces carry rhythm without instrument strings.

sketches.name: Lifted Surface
sketches.idea: A covering sweeps upward into one lifted fold, making shelter and expression arise from the same surface.
construction: A broad curved covering rises from a low left edge into one high fold.
The two end faces reveal the thickness and turn of the same surface.
A large opening below the covering is actual transparent space, with no attached praise icon.
sketches.risk: Its shelter reading is clear, but it overlaps the broader canopy territory; the rise can suggest a sail or performance venue.
sketches.why: An expressive one-gesture alternative, set aside if the joined-covering territory already supplies the stronger and more distinctive version.
sketches.reason: Set aside: the lifted covering overlaps the stronger dwelling premise in 01; the enclosing fold also risks a page/app icon.

sketches.name: Shared Line
sketches.idea: The first T becomes the common structure holding the full name together.
sketches.approach: Custom structural initial plus full-name serif wordmark
sketches.construction: Purpose-drawn initial T: 21-unit overhead beam, one stem, serif base; remaining Source Serif 4 outlines at weight 550 / optical size 24. The two lines read T + abernacle / of Praise. Every visible letter belongs to the name.
sketches.risk: The long T can suggest a signboard or an overbearing roof; the oversized initial changes reading order. A wide wordmark has no automatically successful compact avatar.
sketches.reason: Advances as the strongest full-name alternative. The actual initial T provides the shared structure, making typography carry the identity.

sketches.name: Lifted Praise
sketches.idea: A steady dwelling-name is answered by a gently rising word of praise.
sketches.approach: Full-name expressive sans wordmark with measured baseline movement
sketches.construction: Bricolage Grotesque outlines at weight 550 / width 100 / optical size 24; the Tabernacle line remains stable. The six Praise letters rise 4.5 canvas units per letter without rotating or distorting their shapes; of remains readable.
sketches.risk: Baseline movement can feel playful or like event typography rather than an enduring church identifier; the name is expressive but not inherently a compact symbol.
sketches.reason: Set aside: the rising baseline risks campaign/event typography. The quieter, shared structural line in 11 offers a clearer long-term premise.

concepts.name: Responsive Cover
concepts.idea: Joined textile folds make a dwelling whose own lifted edges express response and praise.
concepts.meaning: Tabernacle is the joined, sheltering textile. Praise is the lift and opening made by that same material. The form is a contemporary interpretation, not a reconstruction of the Exodus tent.
construction: Four curved textile faces define one generous interior; the middle is a real open counter.
Diagonal breaks make folding and coupling visible; nothing is added inside as a second religious icon.
The silhouette is low and broad. No meaning is assigned to the number of pieces.
concepts.risk: The white opening may suggest a robed figure or flame; the draped silhouette can suggest a tent venue or sails. Fine fold tips soften at micro sizes, and praise is less explicit than dwelling.
concepts.longevity: A recognizable draped silhouette could become an enduring identifier if its alternate venue/sail reading is acceptable. It needs name recognition and material proofing.
concepts.smallSize: The main interior survives 24–32px. At 16px the finest tapered folds lose distinction; a separately reviewed micro cut would be required for critical tiny use.

type.rationale: The humanist serif supplies dignity and warmth beside the broad draped mass. Equal-sized name lines preserve the phrase; shaped kerning and deliberate spacing are retained. These are review outlines, not a final wordmark.

concepts.name: Common Ground
concepts.idea: Unequal broad surfaces depend on one another to make a single generous room; gathering creates the dwelling.
concepts.meaning: Distinct surfaces depend on each other to make one shared room. The gathering creates the dwelling; varied contours suggest collective participation rather than a single performer.
construction: Four unequal broad surfaces surround one shared interior and a substantial front opening.
The surfaces rise and turn around the center; their relationship is the symbol rather than separate people or heads.
A fine overlap crease is secondary. The room and opening must remain recognizable when that crease closes small.
concepts.risk: May read as an architectural/cultural institution rather than a church. The fine left crease closes small; do not assign doctrinal meaning to the number of surfaces.
concepts.longevity: The stable shared-room silhouette is promising for recognition across sign, screen, and paper. An independent reader test should establish whether it feels warm and ecclesial.
concepts.smallSize: The shared interior and broad front opening remain visible at 16–32px. The secondary left crease closes at the smallest sizes, so it must not carry the core meaning.

type.rationale: Open sans letterforms keep the full name welcoming and legible beside the more expressive spatial form. The calmer type lets the room carry the character; line lengths are accepted instead of stretching lowercase.
type.license: SIL Open Font License 1.1. Original fonts, copyright and exact OFLs retained under assets/fonts/. No font binary is modified; no typography system is approved.

concepts.name: Cadenced Wall
concepts.idea: A folded wall changes height and turns around a shared forecourt; the structure itself carries an expressive cadence.
concepts.meaning: A folded architectural wall gathers around an implied forecourt. Its changing heights and intervals make the dwelling itself expressive: praise as cadence, with no musical instrument.
construction: Five broad filled faces turn through a measured sequence, keeping a visible relationship to folded construction.
Major seams are at least 12 units on the 256-unit canvas. There are no hairline strings or white overlays.
The lower edges hold an implied forecourt; changing height creates the cadence. Piece count is compositional.
concepts.risk: Could suggest a cultural venue, performance hall, or skyline. Rhythm is a creative association with praise; architecture alone cannot establish worship.
concepts.longevity: Its distinctive broad sequence could become recognizable at sign and header scale. A successful compact cut is still needed before it could cover every digital use.
concepts.smallSize: At 24–64px the fold sequence is visible. At 16px the articulation weakens into a segmented skyline; this is an unresolved limitation, not a passed favicon.

type.rationale: The serif counters the harder architectural edges with a human voice. The full name remains at the same type size and spacing logic as the other symbol tests, so the folded wall is judged on its own merits.
type.license: SIL Open Font License 1.1. Original fonts, copyright and exact OFLs retained under assets/fonts/. No font binary is modified; no typography system is approved.

concepts.name: Shared Line
concepts.idea: The first T becomes the common structure holding the full name together.
concepts.meaning: The initial T becomes a common overhead structure and anchor for the complete name. “of Praise” inhabits that same typographic structure: the words carry the meaning without a separate icon.
construction: A purpose-drawn initial T uses a 16-unit common beam, tapered ends, and a flared stem; Source Serif 4 weight 550 / optical size 24 provides the other letter outlines. Native kerning is retained. The horizontal arrangement uses the same grammar with a shorter stem; it does not stretch the text.
The two-line and true single-line compositions share a drawn initial and licensed Source Serif 4 outlines. The font binary is not modified.
The compact T is only a provisional derived initial; the full wordmark carries more recognition.
concepts.risk: The long overhead line may read as a signboard or roof. The compact T has weaker distinctiveness without the full name. The single-line arrangement is very wide; minimum sizes and final clear space are not established.
concepts.longevity: The complete name offers immediate verbal identification and a typographic route to long-term recognition. Its oversized T and roof-like beam need reader testing; the compact initial is less distinctive.
concepts.smallSize: The compact T is tested separately at 64–16px. The complete wordmark is tested at 320/240px width; it is not claimed to be readable at 16px.

compact.label: Provisional derived T / compact test
compact.caution: The compact T is less distinctive without the full name. It is a companion hypothesis, not an approved standalone emblem.

type.family: Source Serif 4 outlines + purpose-drawn initial T
type.rationale: The initial is constructed to hold the two readable name lines; other letters retain their licensed humanist shapes and actual kerning. The lighter developed beam gives the ascenders room. A single-line horizontal version uses the same grammar.
type.license: SIL Open Font License 1.1. Original fonts, copyright and exact OFLs retained under assets/fonts/. No font binary is modified; no typography system is approved.

sources.title: Exodus 25:8–9 — sanctuary and dwelling among the people
sources.note: WEB public-domain text, identified third-party mirror. Exact selected verses and response hash retained locally; no claim of publisher-hosted retrieval.

sources.title: Exodus 40:34–38 — cloud, glory, and the journey
sources.note: Text describes presence and journey. It supplies no prescribed logo for God.

sources.title: Psalm 100:1–5 — entering, thanksgiving, and praise
sources.note: Read in its own worship setting. Its courts are not treated as an Exodus architectural diagram.

sources.title: Psalm 150 — many expressions, all breath
sources.note: Multiple instruments and bodily expression prevent a compulsory harp-only interpretation of praise.

sources.title: Hebrews 9 — earthly sanctuary and Christological argument
sources.note: Restricted ancient access and the argument of the chapter are retained; a floorplan is not a complete Christian identity statement.

sources.title: Exodus 26–27 / Numbers 4 — joined construction and portability
sources.note: Primary textual description: coupled textiles, coverings, frames, screens, and court. Archaeological dating or a precise historical reconstruction was not independently verified; scholarly site retrieval was blocked.

sources.note: Source Serif 4, Instrument Sans, and Bricolage Grotesque were inspected in the complete name. Original variable fonts, OFLs, metadata, and checksums are retained.

selectionNotes: The four develop different kinds of identifier: a draped covering, a shared spatial enclosure, a broad architectural cadence, and a full-name wordmark. Selection favors a visible relationship to the name, silhouette distinction, and credible reproduction. The other eight remain visible with specific reasons. This is a development shortlist for your review, not a selection of the church’s identity.
